3. It has been stated in the writ petition as well as in the supplementary affidavits that the learned Judge of the Adalat passed the impugned order illegally inasmuch as, the last execution case was filed by the Bank after 2 years 10 months 23 days from the date of disposal of the previous execution case and so, it is barred by limitation in view of the provision of section 28 of the Ain; that the application filed by the Bank for execution of the decree is not supported by any affidavit or verification and it was not signed by any authority of the decree-holder-Bank and, as such, order for civil custody/warrant of arrest cannot be issued against the petitioners under section 34 of the Ain; that the impugned order is thus unlawful and liable to be struck down. 

 4. Respondent No.1, the Bank contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the suit was filed for recovery of loan impleading the petitioners as defendants of the suit and the petitioners are borrowers and personal guarantors for the loan. The suit was lawfully decreed against the defendant-petitioners as they did not contest the suit. The judgment-debtor-petitioners having failed to pay the decretal dues, the Bank law- fully filed the execution case against them for recovery of the decretal dues. The application was filed by the Bank for Civil detention and issuing warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors lawfully as the mortgaged property could not be sold in auction. The first, the second and the last execution case are not barred by limitation. The writ petition is vague and thus, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 5. Mr Md Osman Ghani Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate for petitioners submits that it has already been settled by this Division in a good number of cases that prior show cause is not necessary before passing order for civil prison and issuing warrant of arrest and therefore, he does not press this question in this writ petition. He next submits that from the materials on record it transpires that first Execution Case No. 50 of 1994 was rejected on 4-6-2000 and the second Execution Case No. 123 of 2000 was rejected on 24-10-2002 and the third execution was filed on 28-4-2003 before the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into operation and, therefore, the third execution case being Decree Execution Case No. 60 of 2003, re-numbered as Artha Jari Case No. 74 of 2003 is not barred by limitation and so, he does not press this question.
